name.en: Fake parking or traffic fine text: “pay now to avoid extra charges”

how.en: A text says you have an unpaid parking fine, an unfinished parking session or an outstanding traffic ticket. It may use the name of a parking company such as RingGo or Parkingeye, or the Department for Transport. A link leads to a fake payment page that takes your card and personal details. The companies and the department say these texts are scams.

text.en: A text says it is from a parking company or the Department for Transport.
It says you have an unpaid fine and extra charges will be added if you don’t pay soon.
It gives a link to “view” or “pay” the fine.
The page asks for your card details.
RingGo: You have an unpaid parking session. Please settle your balance today to avoid an additional penalty charge: [link]
DfT: Our records show an outstanding traffic violation ticket. Pay now to avoid further action: [link]

en: text about an unpaid parking fine
A fine you didn’t know about, sent by text with a link.
A threat of extra charges if you don’t pay today.
A sender number or address that has nothing to do with the company.
Don’t click the link. Check for unpaid sessions in the official RingGo app or website, or on the paperwork you received.
If you paid, call your bank straight away (you can dial 159).
